passage:
Day 1. Hafsa said she couldn't skip her cousin's engagement dinner on Saturday. Noor's reply came fast: "So I don't matter. You're selfish. I'll fall apart without you." Hafsa's chest tightened. She typed three apologies and deleted them. She felt she had done something terrible.

Day 5. She gave in and told her mother she was ill. The whole evening she watched Noor's messages and felt hollow, not relieved. Noor was warm again, and Hafsa noticed how the warmth came only after she gave in.

Day 12. When Noor started again about another plan, Hafsa wrote, "I care about you, and I'm still going." It hurt. She went to Ms Iyer, the school counsellor, and told her all of it. "You can be kind to Noor and still say no," Ms Iyer said. "Let's keep talking."

qa.q: Which event did Hafsa say she could not skip on Day 1?
qa.a: She could not skip her cousin's engagement dinner on Saturday.

qa.q: How did Hafsa feel after giving in on Day 5?
qa.a: Hollow, not relieved. She noticed that Noor's warmth only came back after she gave in.

qa.q: What did Hafsa do differently on Day 12?
qa.a: She wrote that she cared but was still going, and she talked to the school counsellor Ms Iyer, which is care without giving in plus help from a trusted adult.

qa.q: How might Noor see the situation?
qa.a: Noor may truly feel scared of losing Hafsa, but pressure that blames her for Noor's feelings is not fair to either of them.

grounding: Noor calls Hafsa selfish and says they will fall apart when she resists; over days she moves from guilt and giving in to caring while holding her ground and seeking a counsellor.

passage:
Afreen, you asked why I went so quiet last term. I'm Rashmi, and I'll tell you now, because maybe it helps you too.
I was going out with Arnav. Whenever I said no to anything, like skipping my dance class to see him, or not replying at midnight, he'd say, "You're so selfish. You don't care about me. I'll fall apart without you."
And I believed it. I felt like his feelings were my job. I cancelled dance three times. I stopped sleeping properly.
One day I cried in the washroom, and our class teacher found me. I told her everything. She took me straight to the school counsellor that afternoon. The counsellor said, "You can care about him and still say no. His feelings are his to manage, with help from adults if he needs it."
She also called my mother that day. Now I still care about Arnav. But I don't miss dance anymore. And I'm sleeping again.

qa.q: How many times did Rashmi cancel dance?
Why did Rashmi feel responsible for Arnav's feelings?
qa.a: Rashmi felt guilty and anxious because Arnav called Rashmi selfish and said he would fall apart, so his feelings seemed like Rashmi's job.

qa.q: Which steps helped Rashmi, and why?
qa.a: Telling the class teacher, seeing the counsellor that afternoon and involving Mum helped Rashmi care about Arnav without giving in.

qa.q: How might Arnav see Rashmi saying no?
qa.a: Arnav seems to feel threatened and upset when Rashmi says no, and uses guilt to keep control instead of handling his own feelings.

grounding: A teen whose partner cries selfishness at every refusal learns to care without giving in, with help from a teacher and counsellor.

passage:
Monday. Varun told Ishita he couldn't come to her cousin's party because of his cricket match. She went silent, then texted: "Fine. I guess I'm not important to you. I'm always the one who sacrifices." Varun felt awful. He skipped the match.
Thursday. When Varun said he needed Friday evening for his grandmother's birthday, Ishita wrote: "You're so selfish. If you leave me alone again, I don't know what I'll do." His chest tightened. He cancelled on his grandmother, and hated himself for it.
Sunday. Varun told his Mama everything over tea at the dhaba near their house. Mama listened, then said, "You can care about her and still keep your plans. Her feelings aren't your job to fix." That same evening Mama helped him call the school counsellor's helpline number, and they agreed he'd see the counsellor on Monday morning.
Varun texted Ishita: "I care about you, but I'm going to my match next week."

qa.q: Why did Varun first say he couldn't come to the party?
How did Varun feel after cancelling on his grandmother?
qa.a: He felt guilty and trapped, as if Ishita's feelings were his responsibility, and hated himself for giving in.

qa.q: What did Varun's Mama advise, and why does it help?
qa.a: To care about Ishita but keep his own plans, since her feelings aren't his to fix; Mama also helped him contact the counsellor the same evening.

qa.q: How might Ishita see Varun keeping his plans?
qa.a: Ishita may feel upset or abandoned at first, since she used guilt to keep him close, but it gives her a chance to face her own feelings.

grounding: A teen whose partner guilt-trips him learns to care without giving in, with help from an uncle and a counsellor.
